CustomField.description: Auto-managed. Do not set on insert from Flow — the system silently overrides to Recurring, producing the misleading error "You can only create a custom schedule when the commitment schedule type is Custom" when a Custom GiftCommitmentSchedule is then attached. Correct Flow pattern: insert GiftCommitment with no ScheduleType, then insert schedule children; ScheduleType populates from the first schedule. Apex can set ScheduleType='Custom' explicitly on insert (required when the child schedule's TransactionPeriod is 'Custom' — mismatch throws "Update the gift commitment schedule type to Recurring or Custom" at GCS insert). ScheduleType populates at insert time (indicates the shape of the attached schedule); the sibling CurrentGiftCmtScheduleId only populates when that schedule's StartDate arrives. A commitment can have ScheduleType set while CurrentGiftCmtScheduleId is still null — future-dated schedule waiting to activate. Allowed values: Recurring, Custom.
CustomField.inlineHelpText: Set to 'Custom' when the payment schedule has irregular installments. Otherwise leave blank — it will populate automatically from the payment schedule's frequency. To check if a schedule is currently active, use the Current Gift Commitment Schedule lookup instead.
